Published online:
    August 31, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Global (primary focus: Middle East/Strait of Hormuz, Europe, US, Japan, New Zealand, Canada)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [NO]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES]

Synopsis:
    US military strikes on Iranian missile positions in the Strait of Hormuz have escalated Gulf tensions, pushing Brent crude above $90/bbl and pressuring global equities. Oil exports remain well below pre-war levels despite escort operations showing some progress. A heavy central bank policy calendar looms: BOJ hike priced at 70% (Sep 18), ECB hike heavily priced (Sep 10), and Fed hike at 58% probability (Sep 16). G20 finance ministers meet with an expected hawkish tone. Japanese 10-year yields hit highest since 1996, tracking a US Treasury selloff. German CPI is the key data point Monday.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: NO — The primary driver is the Gulf conflict and oil prices, with US rates as a significant but secondary thread.

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 65 (moderately relevant — a Fed hike is explicitly discussed as the forward scenario)
Probability of increase: 58%

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 35 (minor — holding is implicitly the alternative to the 58% hike probability)
Probability of holding: 42%

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (NO — cuts are not mentioned or implied anywhere in the article)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 65 (More hawkish than before — $90 oil, sticky inflation pressures, G20 tone expected hawkish, Fed hike probability at 58%, and Treasury yields at multi-decade highs all point to a tighter-for-longer posture with upside rate risk)
